column1: # Amendments to moon-regolith-simulants-oxides.tsv, the LUNAR composition table of
#   Regolith simulant dataset under simulated terrestrial and extraterrestrial conditions,
#   Laser-induced Breakdown Spectroscopy. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21639060, CC BY 4.0.
# The table beside this file is the publication's own, transcribed and never edited. Four
# defects were found in it on 19 October 2026 by setting the data set's three routes to the
# same composition against each other, and every row below is one of those defects, with the
# figure as published, the figure to use, and the section that authorised the change:
#   internals/libs/16-GROUND-TRUTH-UNCERTAINTY.md, section 4.
# How to read a row. "cell" replaces one figure and is refused unless the published column is
# what the table actually holds, so this ledger cannot stop describing the data it amends.
# "not-reported" is the absence of a figure, which is never a zero. "recipe" and "premise"
# change nothing and are there to be read: a recipe whose declared components are wrong, and a
# claim the data set asserts without measuring it.
# This ledger is for the LUNAR table only. The martian table of the same publication uses the
# name Na2O-AL for a different sample (JEZ-1 + MGS-1), so a ledger pointed at the wrong table
# would silently give a martian mixture a lunar correction. The martian table was checked for
# the same four classes of defect and carries two of them: one mistyped cell, MgO of K2O-AM,
# 3.004 pp from what its recipe gives, and that name collision. Its iron is NOT mislabelled,
# because its mixtures report Fe2O3 and FeO in the two rows that hold them, so the relabelling
# below has no martian counterpart. Nothing of it is carried as a fixture here, so there is
# nothing to amend; section 4 of the document records the martian defects.

column1: # 2. Section 4.2. Four mixtures are each built with LHS-1E, the one end-member reporting its
# iron as Fe2O3 while the others report FeO, so their published figure adds an Fe2O3 per cent
# to an FeO per cent and no reading of the heading recovers the iron. Section 4.2 gives the
# iron each actually contains, in grams per hundred grams of material, computed from the
# components and the masses weighed out. It is carried here as the two rows the components
# themselves fill, the ferric from LHS-1E and the ferrous from the other part, which
# reproduces that figure to its last digit and gets the oxygen bound to the iron right as
# well. Four decimals because these figures are computed, not measured, and three would move
# the iron by 0.001 pp.
